newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's main enemy is within, ex-KGB head says.
newsitem.headline: Russia's main enemy is within, ex-KGB head says.

text.p: The former head of the Soviet KGB who spent a lifetime spying for Moscow said on Wednesday that Russia's main enemies today were internal and pointed the finger at the current government.

"From my point of view, our main opponents now come from within," Vladimir Kryuchkov, who headed the Soviet Committee for State Security (KGB) from 1988 to 1991, told reporters during a rare public appearance.
"In looking at who is the main enemy in Russia, we must look here, inside Russia, at our society and our government," he said. "The roots of evil are here in Russia."

Kryuchkov, 73, was sacked and arrested after taking part in the failed hardline communist coup against Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev in August 1991. He devoted much of his career to foreign espionage during the Cold War.
He singled out the current Russian government in his remarks on the country's main internal enemy.

"They tell us that the regime gave us freedom, but how can we speak of freedom when there have been millions of victims, who have either perished in wars or street crime by bandits, or those who were not born -- the death rate exceeds the birth rate by a million people a year," he said.
Kryuchkov made his remarks at a press conference attended by several former top officials of the KGB to discuss Russia's national security interests.
